assessments.summary: The supplied argument establishes both parts internally. The finite-block telescope, Fano endpoint bounds, induced-law factorization, fixed encoder map, and all four compatible rate rows are correctly derived for deterministic private-message codes. The explicit finite entropic witness satisfies the stated coarse BSSC entropy, independence, encoding, Markov, dependence-balance, BEC, and scalar support constraints, attains both objective branches at 2h_2(1/4)-5/4, and remains feasible under universally valid finite-variable information inequalities and any finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions.
scopeQualifications: The displayed Fano formula is literal for message alphabet sizes N_1,N_2 at least 2; singleton messages require a harmless separate convention.
The induced auxiliaries have blocklength-dependent alphabets, so the finite-block result is not itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region.
The entropy witness is an actual finite distribution but not an actual binary-input BSSC distribution: X is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components.

The no-go result applies only to the specified coarse entropy/universal-inequality/finite-copy relaxation; exact binary-posterior and other channel-specific consistency constraints may exclude the witness.
The conclusion is an obstruction to that refinement route, not a broadcast-channel capacity bound.
evidenceIssues: No objective execution attestations were supplied; validity rests on the self-contained analytic derivations and direct verification of the witness construction rather than trusted checker output.
